index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents a flow diagram of a biofertilizer production process, structured as a closed-loop system integrating anaerobic digestion, biogas utilization, wastewater treatment, and solid recovery. The global layout is divided into two main vertical streams: the upper section handles biogas processing and energy generation, while the lower section manages liquid and solid waste treatment and biofertilizer production. The diagram flows from left to right and top to bottom, with feedback loops connecting the treatment units to the bioreactor.

Visual modules include gray rectangular or cylindrical tanks for processing units such as the Anaerobic Digester, Compressor, Combustor, Turbine, Dryer, and Pressure Filter. The b-PBR (biological Photobioreactor) is depicted as a multi-tube reactor with blue liquid and green algal biomass inside, indicating active biological growth. The Flocculation Tank and Lamella Clarifier are shown as blue tanks with internal mixing and settling zones, respectively. The Solids-Liquids Separator is a conical funnel with internal slats. Makeup Water is represented by a blue oval tank with wavy lines. Inputs like Manure, Air, Urea, and Blowdown are labeled with arrows entering the system. Outputs include CH4, Flue Gas, Biofertilizer, and Purge streams.

Connections and arrows indicate material and energy flows. Manure enters the Anaerobic Digester, producing biogas that passes through an H2S Scrubber and CO2 Scrubber to remove impurities, yielding purified CH4. This methane is compressed and combusted with air to drive a turbine, generating electricity, with flue gas as a byproduct. The digester effluent flows to the Solids-Liquids Separator, which splits it into bedding solids and liquid. The bedding is sent to a Dryer, producing Biofertilizer as output, with blowdown recycled back to the system. The liquid stream enters the b-PBR, where it is enriched with Urea and Makeup Water to support algal growth. The b-PBR effluent goes to the Flocculation Tank, then to the Lamella Clarifier, and finally to the Pressure Filter. The filtered liquid is recirculated to the b-PBR as a purge stream, while the solid residue from the filter is returned to the b-PBR as a recycle stream. The entire system emphasizes resource recovery and closed-loop operation, minimizing waste and maximizing reuse.
